stem: The sum of three consecutive integers is less than 40. What is the greatest possible value of the largest of the three integers?
solution: Let the integers be \(n\), \(n + 1\) and \(n + 2\). Their sum is \(3n + 3\).
\(3n + 3 < 40\) gives \(3n < 37\), so \(n < 12.33\); the greatest integer \(n\) is 12.
The largest of the three integers is \(n + 2 = 14\). Check: \(12 + 13 + 14 = 39 < 40\), while \(13 + 14 + 15 = 42\) is too big.
verify:
best = max(n for n in range(-100, 100) if 3*n + 3 < 40)
assert best == 12 and best + 2 == 14
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [14]
